title: Wathan Sentencing
full_story:
Clay County State’s Attorney Phillip M. Givens announced that Jeffrey M. Wathan, 26, of Xenia, was sentenced to time in the Illinois Department of Corrections on Wednesday, in Clay County Circuit Court for violating the terms and conditions of probation.

Wathan was previously placed on 24 months of probation for Aggravated Domestic Battery, a Class 2 Felony, on February 24, of 2025.  He was ordered to complete substance abuse counseling as part of the terms and conditions of his probation.  Wathan admitted to violating that term and condition on and was sentenced to 4 years and 6 months in the Illinois Department of Corrections on Wednesday.  He will have to serve 85% of that sentence with a 4-year period of Mandatory Supervised Release to follow.

The case was investigated by the Flora Police Department and the violation of probation handled by the Clay County Probation Office.  State’s Attorney Phillip Givens said: “This is another example of a defendant not taking advantage of the opportunity to become a productive member of the community.  We want defendants to take substance abuse counseling seriously to better their lives.  If they do not, then we will continue to hold people accountable.  I am grateful to have such experienced Probation Officers and dedicated Law Enforcement when it comes to accountability.”

title: CCH LAB FAIR
full_story:
Clay County Hospital and Medical Clinics will be hosting their popular “Reduced Rate Lab Fair” beginning October 15th through October 31st.  You may at any time pick up a voucher at Clay County Hospital, or any CCH clinic including Flora, Louisville and Clay City during regular business hours.

The blood draws must be completed October 15th through October 31st.  The hours for the blood draws are Monday through Friday, from 7 am till 7 pm and Saturdays from 7 am till 11 am at the Clay County Hospital.  Please complete your voucher before registering.  Payment is due at registration.

Regular blood tests are an essential part of your preventative health care plan.  Multiple choices of labs are available for you to select on the voucher.  The popular “Lab Fair Panel” results include the kidney and liver functions, complete blood count, and measure cholesterol levels and triglycerides.  Clay County Hospital and Medical Clinics thanks you for choosing them as your choice of healthcare and they look forward to serving you during the “Reduced Rate Lab Fair” October 15th through October 31st.

title: MITIGATION PLANNING COMMITTEE MEETING
full_story:
Mitigation projects and activities that can reduce injuries and fatalities while maintaining vital services for Clay County residents will be the main topic of discussion at the upcoming Clay County Hazard Mitigation Planning Committee meeting.  The meeting will be held at the Clay County Health Department, 601 E. 12th Street, in Flora, at 1 pm on Wednesday.

The Committee began work in January to update the county’s Natural Hazards Mitigation Plan.  This plan details the past severe weather events that have impacted the County and identifies mitigation projects and activities that can be taken before an event occurs to protect residents and critical services and infrastructure.

“Obtaining FEMA’s approval of our updated Plan will make all of the participants eligible to apply for federal grant money for mitigation projects and activities,” said Flora-Clay County Emergency Services and Disaster Agency Coordinator, Steve Lewis.

Building community safe rooms, acquiring flood prone properties, resolving drainage issues, retrofitting critical infrastructure to better withstand hazard events, installing back-up power supplies, and developing public information materials are a few of the mitigation projects more commonly proposed in Illinois.

Projects identified by Committee members at this meeting will become part of the County’s updated Plan.  While the committee has provided input on portions of the Plan, the Plan will be presented in full for public review and comment before it is submitted to the state and federal government for approval.

“A public forum will be conducted after the first of the year for interested persons to review the Plan update and ask questions of Committee Members.  A two-week public comment period will be held following the public forum to accommodate interested residents who are unable to attend.  We want to make sure that anybody who is interested has an opportunity to review and comment on the draft Plan update,” added Lewis.

Interested persons can submit questions and comments to the Flora-Clay County Emergency Services and Disaster Agency office.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
The American Red Cross is appealing for blood and platelet donors of all blood types to schedule donation appointments this fall.  The organization provides more than 6.5 million blood products to hospitals nationwide each year.

There will be a Blood Drive on Tuesday in the Link Gymnasium of the Blue Point Free Will Baptist Church from Noon to 6 pm.  Donors who give blood or platelets before October 18th will receive a $15 e-gift card to a merchant of their choice.

To be eligible to donate, individuals must be at least 17 years old, or 16 with parental consent, where permitted by state law and weigh at least 110 pounds while in generally good health.  High school students and other donors 18 years of age and younger must also meet specific height and weight requirements.  Donors must present a blood donor card, driver’s license or two other forms of identification at check-in.

Appointments can be made using the Red Cross Blood Donor App, by visiting RedCrossBlood.org, by calling 1-800-RED CROSS or by enabling the Blood Donor Skill on Alexa Echo devices.  Donors can use RapidPass online on the day of their appointment to complete pre-donation reading and health history questionnaires before arriving.

The next Blood Drive in Flora will be on Thursday, October 15th from Noon to 5 pm at the Flora Church of the Nazarene.  There will also be a Blood Drive on Thursday, October 29th at the Clay City High School from 1 to 5 pm.

title: Nite Patrol Results
full_story:
Illinois State Police (ISP) Troop 9 Commander, Captain Bruce Waggoner, announced the results of Nighttime Enforcement (NITE) patrols in Clay, Effingham, Fayette, Hamilton, Marion, Wayne and White counties during August and September.  These NITE patrols allowed the ISP to focus on preventing, detecting, and taking enforcement action in response to impaired driving and occupant restraint violations especially between the hours of 9:00 pm and 6:00 am.

During the month officers wrote 6 citations for Driving under the influence and 9 other alcohol or drug citations.  There were also 24 registration offenses, and 2 occupant restraint offenses.  There were also 92 speeding violations issued and 18 drivers license offenses.

Alcohol and drug impairment are estimated to be a factor in more than 47% of all fatal motor vehicle crashes in Illinois.  There is one alcohol-related traffic fatality every 39 minutes in the United States.  Over half of all fatal crashes in Illinois occur at night.  The NITE program allows officers to work even harder at removing dangerous impaired drivers from the road and making sure everyone is buckled up.  This project was funded through the Illinois Department of Transportation.

title: HUNTERS REMINDED ABOUT CWD
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) is reminding deer hunters about locations where deer can be tested for chronic wasting disease (CWD) free of charge.

Chronic wasting disease is a fatal disease of the central nervous system in deer and elk. It was first detected in a suspect adult female deer from northwest Boone County in 2002. Since 2002, 199,136 wild deer have been sampled statewide, with 3,410 testing positive for CWD.   The disease is currently confined to a 28-counties in Illinois.

Wildlife biologists monitor the geographic distribution and intensity of CWD primarily through testing of hunter-harvested deer. CWD is not known to be transmissible to humans; however, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the World Health Organization do not recommend consuming CWD-positive venison.

Salt and Strings Butchery in Louisville is a CWD sampling station, taking samples from entire deer or deer heads thru January 17th.  Hunters can view the results of their CWD tests online.  Please allow two to four weeks for results to post. Priority is given to samples from counties with known CWD cases.  Hunters will be contacted by an IDNR wildlife biologist if their deer tests positive for CWD.
